one_line_contribution: That the reported gain of trajectory retrieval over a fixed exemplar prompt in an LLM agent should be scored against the distribution of fixed prompts you could have drawn from the same bank rather than against one draw, with the concrete claim that on ALFWorld retrieval lands at an upper quantile of that draw distribution and is recoverable by a query-free curation rule (shortest successful trajectory per type).
closest_prior_work: Two, one for the mechanism and one for the domain. (a) VERIFIED: Lu et al., 'Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them' (arXiv:2104.08786, ACL, 1672 citations; verified via s2cli paper lookup). It established precisely the proposal's structure in the ICL home literature: the spread of task performance across draws/permutations of the same few-shot set spans near-SOTA to near-chance and exceeds the gain reported by the selection methods of the day, and it then recovers the top of that distribution with a query-free, held-out selection rule. The proposal's Related Work gestures at this as 'prompt-order sensitivity' without citing or verifying it, which understates the threat: P1 (draw SD dominates seed SD) and the P4 curation-rule claim are the agent-trajectory restatement of that paper's two results. What is genuinely not in it: multi-turn agent trajectories, a paired same-bank fixed-vs-retrieved contrast (E3), and locating a retriever as a quantile rather than a mean. That residual is real but thin for a main-track novelty claim. (b) VERIFIED: Traj-Bootstrap, 'Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks' (arXiv:2505.00234, NeurIPS 2025, 19 citations; verified). The proposal characterizes it accurately — it exploits database-to-database variance under always-on retrieval and never runs a fixed no-retriever draw — so it bounds rather than kills the contribution. Nearest recent adjacent work I found and verified: 'On Randomness in Agentic Evals' (arXiv:2602.07150, 7 citations), which documents large run-to-run variance in agentic evaluation but does not decompose it into exemplar-draw versus seed versus game components, and does not locate retrieval within it.
strongest_objection: The proposal's own binding measurement makes the headline branch nearly arithmetically unavailable, and the proposal never says so. Measurement C gives k3 - static3 = +17.2 net [11.9, 22.4], where static3 is a type-conditioned three-exemplar fixed draw — i.e. one sample from exactly the lottery E1 enumerates. For the title's claim to survive, the held-out best of 16 draws must close at least 9.2 of those 17.2 net (P2's 8-net tolerance). With 16 draws the expected max sits about 1.75 SD above the draw mean, so this requires a true draw SD of roughly 5-6 net against a per-draw sampling SE of about 2 net — a draw-variance component three times sampling noise, on a six-template environment whose within-type expert trajectories the proposal itself concedes are procedurally near-identical. The far more likely outcome is the narrow-lottery branch, in which the paper reports that a fixed agent prompt is robust to the draw and retrieval's +17.2 is a genuine mean shift: a careful confirmation of the status quo, with the title's claim dead and the contribution reduced to a reporting recommendation. A reviewer will also note that P1 and P5 pull against each other — a draw SD large enough to satisfy P1 predicts that within-bank exemplar choice matters a great deal, which is hard to square with P5's prediction that same-bank retrieval beats a same-bank fixed draw by less than 8 net — and that the entailment check already marks P2 and P3 unresolvable at the stated power (E5 evaluates on a quarter grid of about 134 episodes with per-arm SE near 4 net against a floor calibrated on 548-episode cells; P3's SD ratio is estimated from 8 draws with a chi-square CI near +-55%). So the headline is both improbable and, as powered, likely to come back undecided.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, all cheap on this node. (1) State the reconciliation as a pre-registered quantity: given the measured +17.2, compute and pre-declare the draw SD required for the best held-out draw to close it, and make that the headline prediction instead of the SD-ratio in P1 — it is the number the claim actually rests on. (2) Add the per-episode random-selection arm (see missing baseline); without it neither P2's 'per-instance information' reading nor P5's paired residual can be interpreted. (3) Fix the power: cross-fit E5 over full seed splits (select the best draw on all 274 seed-1 cells, evaluate on all 274 seed-2 cells, average with the mirror) rather than quartering the grid, or restate E5's floor at about +-16; run 16 self-pool draws instead of 8 so P3's F-test has df 15,15 and pre-register the SD ratio (about 2x) that separates it from 1.0. (4) Turn the two incomparable bank points into a manipulation: run the 80-item bank sample as a ladder (6 / 80 / 1,465) with the whole-bank-in-context arm at 80, so 'the residual shrinks when the bank shrinks' is measured as a curve rather than inferred from a single 80-item comparison against a 1,465-item one. With (1)-(4) the paper answers a sharp question — how much of retrieval's +17.2 is selection, how much is per-instance matching, and how much is bank size — under either outcome, instead of resting on a branch the node's own data disfavors.
missing_baseline: A per-episode random exemplar draw: three type-matched successful trajectories resampled independently for every episode, token-matched to k=3 and left uncached like the retrieval arms (548 episodes, about 30 min). Every fixed arm in the plan holds its exemplars constant across all 548 episodes while every retrieval arm varies them per episode, so E3's paired R_b - F_b residual confounds query-matching with per-episode variety, and P2's falsifier ('retrieval carries per-instance information beyond exemplar choice') has no non-informative per-instance control to be measured against. This is the standard random-per-instance baseline that the kNN-demonstration literature the proposal cites uses, and its omission is the first thing a reviewer of that literature will name. Secondary omission: the round's own binding rule requires a whole-bank-in-context arm wherever the bank fits 16k, and E3 constructs 80-item banks — about 11k tokens at the brief's 140 tokens/item — yet runs only F_b and R_b on them, never all 80 in context.
preprint_collision: No verified collision; the proposal's own check is above average for this round but its home-literature reading is too shallow, and I judge that a weakness rather than a neutral. Queries I ran, all through the s2cli channel (s2+hf both reporting ok; WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch never used): (1) mechanism, no recency, 'variance of in-context demonstration selection random draws versus retrieval best fixed exemplar set' -> 12 hits, closest 2506.04579 (gradient-matching many-shot selection), 2405.16122 (EASE, ordering-aware exemplar selection), 2309.07900, 2406.10229 (benchmark variance), 2102.09690 (calibrate-before-use); none places a retriever as a quantile of a fixed-prompt draw distribution. (2) mechanism, --recent, 'retrieval gain over randomly sampled fixed demonstrations distribution of prompt performance across sampled example sets' -> 3 hits (2601.21759, 2509.16189, 2502.11027), none relevant; reported as empty on the mechanism. (3) closest named method, --recent, 'self-generated in-context examples trajectory database selection ALFWorld agent variance across databases' -> 2505.00234 (Traj-Bootstrap), 2605.16986 (Skills on the Fly), 2605.05413 (constant-context skill learning); none runs a fixed no-retriever draw distribution. (4) 'retrieved demonstrations do not outperform best randomly chosen fixed demonstration set true few-shot prompt selection held-out' -> 2102.09690, 2506.04579, 2603.26775, 2412.12157; classification only, nothing on agent trajectories. (5) --recent, 'exemplar choice lottery prompt variance embodied agent few-shot trajectory prompts seed variance reporting' -> 2602.07150 'On Randomness in Agentic Evals' (verified, 7 citations), the nearest recent threat: it establishes that agentic eval variance is large enough to invalidate single-run comparisons, but it attributes that to trajectory divergence from sampling, not to exemplar choice, and never contrasts retrieval with a draw distribution. Adjacent, not a collision. ID verification: I verified 2505.00234 (NeurIPS 2025, 19 cit), 2406.14596 (ICAL, NeurIPS, 61 cit), 2605.24117 (SkillEvolBench, 1 cit), 2512.04106 (FLLM 2025, 2 cit), plus 2104.08786 and 2602.07150 which I introduced; all resolve as the proposal describes them. I could not verify 2603.21520 (MemAPO) or 2604.07487 (CLEAR) — the lookup call timed out and I did not retry; they are cited in the brief rather than load-bearing for the proposal's novelty argument. The gap in the proposal's check: its home-vocabulary query returned only recent selection-method papers and it concluded 'none locates retrieval in the draw distribution of a fixed set' without engaging the canonical result that does most of that work on classification (2104.08786), which it mentions only as an unnamed, uncited 'prompt-order sensitivity' line. A collision check that does not verify the strongest classical threat has not established novelty against it.
